CVE-2026-119923.title: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in Babelfish for PostgreSQL TDS Prelogin Parser
CVE-2026-119923.description:
A heap-based buffer overflow in the TDS prelogin parser in the Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 1.0-1.5, 2.1-2.15, 3.1-3.12, 4.0-4.8, 5.1-5.4 and in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands as the database process user via a specially crafted malformed TDS prelogin packet to the TDS port. This record consolidates a related NULL-pointer-dereference finding in the same prelogin parser.

To remediate this issue, we recommend users upgrade to Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 4.10, 5.6, 6.1 or later. As a workaround, restrict network access to the TDS port (default 1433). Customers using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish should upgrade their cluster to Aurora PostgreSQL 13.9.16 (1.5.5), 13.23.3 (1.17.2), 14.6.16 (2.3.5), 14.17.8 (2.12.4), 14.18.6 (2.13.3), 14.19.5 (2.14.2), 14.20.5 (2.15.2), 14.22.3 (2.16.1), 14.23.1 (2.17.0), 15.10.8 (3.8.4), 15.12.8 (3.9.4), 15.13.6 (3.10.3), 15.14.5 (3.11.2),…

CVE-2026-120761.title: Apache Axis2/Java: XML External Entity (XXE) injection via imported WSDL/XSD documents
CVE-2026-120761.description: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. When a client built an AxisService from a WSDL URL, through ServiceClient or AxisService.createClientSideAxisService, wsdl4j import resolution was enabled and the documents named by wsdl:import and xsd:import were parsed by wsdl4j's own XML parser, which processes DOCTYPE declarations and external entities. An attacker who controls a WSDL, or a document it imports, could therefore read local files or make the JVM issue network requests. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-16659.description:
MCUboot's serial-recovery image-upload handler bs_upload() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c declares const struct flash_area *fap = NULL and assigns it only via flash_area_open() part-way through the function. Two early validation failures (goto out_invalid_data) — a CBOR map that fails to decode, or an upload packet missing the off/data members — branch past the open while fap is still NULL, then fall into the shared epilogue. In MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES builds that epilogue unconditionally calls boot_handle_enc_fw(fap), which reaches boot_image_load_header() and flash_area_read() and dereferences the NULL flash_area.

CVE-2026-99360.title: NFSD: Set nn->cld_net before registering the cld pipe
CVE-2026-99360.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Set nn->cld_net before registering the cld pipe

rpc_mkpipe_dentry() instantiates the pipe's dentry before it returns,
so the cld pipe can be opened as soon as nfsd4_cld_register_net() has
run. __nfsd4_init_cld_pipe() does not store the new cld_net in
nn->cld_net until after that call. cld_pipe_downcall() reaches the
cld_net only through that pointer and takes cn_lock without checking
it, so a write() that lands in the window oopses.

Store nn->cld_net once @cn is fully initialized and before the pipe is
registered, and clear it again when registration fails.
